dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (register Y-THIN, chosen by the owner on 23 November 2026 and amended the same night with the owner's choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks, and by at least 4; the eligible items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted (14 in 1781), and the others are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (a target, not a quota); one affair's items are handled as in X-1800-01; the eligible items not chosen are listed here.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1781 has 7 catalogue series, which are 6 papers (C-04): the Portsmouth New-Hampshire Gazette under two catalogue numbers (sn83025584 to 3 September, sn83025585 from 8 September). The Royal Gazette of Charleston survives from March; 5 or 6 papers are in print in any three weeks, so an item needs 4 papers all year.

dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1781 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 653 items printed somewhere, 245 in 4 or more catalogue series by the finder's count), and the families of 1780 were looked for on the 1781 pages (items_from_1780.json: 45 items, 5 in 4 or more). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by machine by about 100 words of its text from the finder's position, over all 1,623 pages in both transcriptions (a dense run of its word 5-grams, at least a quarter of them); the counts were joined into documents (items standing together on most of the same pages). The admitted and chosen items were counted again by about 70 words from their own opening (counts_1781.json), and the pages that only quote or recite them were read and left out. Each admitted printing was checked against its page scan.
